public_rationale: He hedges this figure. He says it "appears" that $200-300 billion of NVIDIA's sales since 2022 are in warehouses or unplugged in data centers waiting for power. He also calls the number of rentable Blackwell chips "questionable." He presents the range as an appearance, not a firm figure, so it is not scored. The evidence gathered also contains no dollar measurement of NVIDIA hardware sold since 2022 that is uninstalled or unpowered. The items below are context only. Yahoo Finance, citing Business Insider on 2026-10-21, reports that Amazon takes ownership of NVIDIA GB300 racks before data centers or power are ready. An internal email projected about $5 billion of deliveries in August 2026 and about $3 billion a month after that. A TIKR column on Yahoo Finance (2026-10-26) said nothing in NVIDIA's sales or in its biggest buyers' statements supports a $200 billion warehouse figure. Epoch AI (published 2026-05-20) modeled deployed compute at the end of 2025 using assumed delivery lags. It said it did not know exactly how much sold compute was operational. None of these items tests the range.
limitations: The context items are news reports, commentary and modeled estimates, not inventory or deployment records.
The Amazon figures are projected deliveries from an internal email, reported secondhand, for one company. They do not show how much hardware stayed unpowered or for how long.
The Epoch estimate is for the end of 2025, not September 2026, and is measured in H100-equivalents, not dollars.
The TIKR column is analyst commentary, not a measurement of idle chips.
The packet found no dollar measure of idle NVIDIA hardware. It does not show whether such a measure exists elsewhere.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: It appears that $200–300 billion of NVIDIA's sales since 2022 are sitting in warehouses or unplugged in data centers waiting for power.

statement.excerpt: While the counterargument might be that Blackwell GPU rental rates aren’t included, as I discussed last week, it’s questionable how many B200, B300, or other Blackwell chips are actually available for rent, as it appears that anywhere from $200 billion to $300 billion of NVIDIA’s sales since 2022 are sitting in warehouses or unplugged in data centers waiting for power.

from_speaker: "sitting in warehouses or unplugged in data centers waiting for power"
framed as making it "questionable how many" Blackwell chips are available for rent
our_interpretation: The speaker hedges twice: it is "questionable" how many Blackwell chips are rentable, and it only "appears" that $200-300B is idle. He offers a rough range he calls an appearance, not a measured fact.
No company, regulator or analyst publishes the dollar value of uninstalled or unpowered NVIDIA hardware, so no public measure exists to test this range against.
Following the earlier reviewers, this hedged estimate is not scored as a firm figure. Context evidence is recorded for readers.
criteria.support_condition: Would be supported only if a credible measurement showed that roughly $200-300B of NVIDIA hardware sold since 2022 was unplugged or warehoused around September 2026. Because the claim is hedged, it is not scored.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Would be contradicted only if a credible measurement showed idle NVIDIA hardware far below $200B around September 2026. Because the claim is hedged, it is not scored.

evidence.excerpt: So, are $200 billion of Nvidia's chips sitting in warehouses? Nothing in Nvidia's sales or what its biggest buyers are saying supports that.
evidence.explanation: An analyst column finds no sign of a $200B glut in NVIDIA's numbers or buyer statements. It is commentary, not a measurement of idle chips.

evidence.excerpt: Amazon is taking ownership of Nvidia GB300 server racks before the data centers or power capacity exist to run them.
evidence.explanation: Shows one large buyer holding NVIDIA racks before power is ready, on the order of billions per month. This is far smaller than the claimed range and covers one company only.

evidence.excerpt: If there’s a one-quarter lag between delivery and deployment, deployed compute at the end of 2025 would be comparable to sold compute as of Q3 2025, which was ~16 million H100e.
evidence.locator: section 'Most AI compute probably doesn't go to frontier AI', paragraph 4
evidence.explanation: Epoch says it does not know how much sold compute is operational and models it with assumed lags. This confirms there is no direct public measure of idle chips.
